\section*{Research experience}
\needspace{6\baselineskip}\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}X r@{}}\textbf{Predoctoral Research Fellow} & {\small July 2025 -- present}\\\end{tabularx}
\emph{Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research (SIEPR)\newline{}TAX Lab, Stanford Graduate School of Business (GSB)}\hfill {\small\color{muted}Palo Alto, CA}\par
Research Fellow under Professors Ran Abramitzky and Rebecca Lester (Stanford GSB).\par
\begin{itemize}
\item Built data pipelines in R, Python, and SQL to support statistical analyses of public and proprietary datasets comprising millions to billions of observations.
\item Developed statistical models for exploratory data analysis and causal inference, examining the impact of economic shocks and various public policies.
\item Translated complex analyses into accessible findings, creating data visualizations, reports, and presentations for both technical and general audiences.
\end{itemize}
\vspace{4pt}
\needspace{6\baselineskip}\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}X r@{}}\textbf{Research Assistant, Economic Policy Studies} & {\small July 2024 -- May 2025}\\\end{tabularx}
\emph{American Enterprise Institute for Public Policy Research (AEI)}\hfill {\small\color{muted}Washington, D.C.}\par
Research Assistant to economists Stan Veuger, Paul Kupiec, and Vincent Smith.\par
\begin{itemize}
\item Built and analyzed economic datasets in Stata, R, and Python to support research on public spending, international food aid, and population change.
\item Applied causal inference methods, including instrumental variables and difference-in-differences, to examine the effects of government policies on economic and political outcomes.
\item Translated technical analyses into accessible findings, contributing tables, visualizations, and written summaries for research papers and policy materials.
\end{itemize}
\vspace{4pt}
\needspace{6\baselineskip}\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}X r@{}}\textbf{Research Assistant} & {\small Nov. 2023 -- June 2024}\\\end{tabularx}
\emph{University of Hawai`i Economic Research Organization (UHERO)}\hfill {\small\color{muted}Honolulu, HI}\par
Research Assistant to economists Dylan Moore, Peter Fuleky, and Rachel Inafuku.\par
\begin{itemize}
\item Analyzed social-network and income data to examine economic inequality in Hawai`i, contributing to a coauthored policy brief.
\item Prepared economic data for quarterly forecasting and academic research, collecting, organizing, and checking inputs for analysis.
\item Produced statistical summaries and visualizations to interpret economic patterns and communicate findings.
\end{itemize}

\section*{Technical skills and languages}
